Early Hack-Cess - The Problem with Steam's Early Access (opinion)

I actually don't have an issue with early access games. Anytime I've bought an early access, I had done my research before hand and found out whether the game was good or bad, at that time of its development. Many of the games are one's that i would buy anyways once it's actually finished so I may as well buy then as an early access to ensure I would get it because I may not have the money later. There are multiple early access games I'm interested in but I didn't get because they are very good right now. As long as you don't blindly buy early access games then it's fine. Just do research on it before hand.
Yes, I think research is the key. I would only do early access for a game I was definitely going to buy.

I, on the other hand, avoid early access games like the plague. There are very, very few games I'll replay. How it's gone with early access for me is that I shell out the dough, play through the content in the current build of the game, say "heh, that was neat," and never open it up again. For my use case, it only makes sense to wait til a game is finished to buy it; if I'm only going on one tour through a game, it should be through the finished game.

This is very frustrating to me, as Steam is littered with early access titles. Since an early access title can advertise based on what they think the finished game will be like as opposed to what it will actually be like or what the current state of the game is, the early access games are usually the ones that stand out and get me excited (usually for a product that doesn't even exist yet).

I wish they were in their own section, separated from the finished games. I got the Steam Enhanced extension because it can hide Early Access games. It just leaves a hole where the game was, and for every 10 games you look at in a list there can be up to four early access games. There's usually one to three in the featured games. I'm glad somebody's enjoying this trend because it's really just not for me.

I understand completely where you are coming from. In all honesty most of the early access games that I'm interested in I don't buy, simply because they are no where near what I hope and expect them to be. Some of the ones I've played were solid. I enjoyed the crap out of Nether while it was in the later stages of its early access, but if it were a story based game I wouldn't buy it. Like you say, no reason to play a game like that while it's being made.
This is a very good point. Early access isn't quite my thing either, but I can see why a lone indie dev would use it for example. Thanks for sharing your POV.

I'm torn on this. Some games (Like The Stomping Land) seem like they offered this way too early in the development cycle, essentially turning the early adopters into alpha testers for their product. Kerbal Space Program, on the other hand, is something I really was happy I did early access on.
I feel the same way. However, after DayZ, I don't think I will be buying any other "early access" game since this early release tends to spoil the game for me.
